evidence.excerpt: In high-volume garment production, fabric is spread in multiple layers before cutting, and rolls of different remaining lengths must be combined to cover the required spread length. Mis-matched roll combinations create tail-end fabric scraps that contribute significantly to total waste. This paper models the multi-layer spread scheduling problem as a set-covering integer program in which columns represent feasible roll combinations for a given required spread length. A Lagrangian relaxation of the coverage constraints is solved iteratively to obtain lower bounds; the relaxed subproblem decomposes into independent knapsack problems solvable in polynomial time. On instances with 20 to 60 active fabric rolls and 8 to 25 cutting orders, the Lagrangian bound closes 89% of the integrality gap on average, and an LP-rounding post-processing step produces near-optimal integer solutions. Applied to three months of production data from a Serbian shirt manufacturer, the method reduces tail-end waste by 14.3% relative to current manual planning.
